My mother and my teens had never been rafting. The teens thought it would be exciting. My mother is checking things of her "end of life is approaching quickly" bucket list, so she asked to tag along.

I take them on an easy river for beginners. Ones and twos with a few threes thrown in. Only one set of rapids poses any real sort of challenge - a small falls.

I have run this river since I was in high school. Have never been bounced. Never had anyone else in my raft fall out either. Never needed to pay a guide on this particular river, because in high school went with more experienced rafters and I know the river quite well.

So what happens? My mother and a (female) teen in front decide they both know better than everyone else. They fight me while I am trying to get us away from a massive submerged rock. We all go in, but we all manage to grab the raft while I catch a couple paddles and toss those into the raft.

Female teen is freaking out and useless. My mother only has one good arm and it is holding tight to the raft. She also has an undisclosed staggering life-long fear of drowning, and her worst nightmare is coming true... so she's basically useless at this point.

I waste seconds fighting panic (not for myself, been in rougher water before) realizing that the falls are approaching quick and I know female teen has no upper body strength and due to freaking out is at real risk in the falls.

I thought my mom was gone at that point. She's really short. Couldn't see her at the back of the raft past the teens. But she's old, so I have bigger problems.

Fortunately teen number 2 is tall. My head reaches his chest. He is able to pull himself nearly into the raft. He's up high enough so a guide sitting by his raft and crew on the opposite river bank can see our raft isn't just floating by empty.

About this time the river bed flattens for a pullout (thanks army corp of engineers), so I am able to put a foot down without breaking it and pivot the raft to have us facing the people at the pull out. The guide throws us a line and my son and I grab and start pulling the raft to shore.

End of story? Should have been. XD We lost two paddles and female teen was still in the middle of a panic attack despite sitting on dry land. So we left the raft at the pullout and hiked back to the outfitters. It wasn't too far away. When we got there, one of the their guides offered to give us more paddles so we could go back and finish.

I was okay with it. Plus I had prepaid for my photo and we hadn't reached the falls where the photographers are set up. Male teen was cool with it. My mom decided that she had already beaten old man river once, so what else could go wrong? Female teen was done. Only 3 rafters? No problem says the outfitter's employee. The raft is only slightly larger than those three-person duckies they rent on this river. Despite my mom having one nearly lame arm, we totally had this. Totally.

And we did, for the most part. We hit the falls at the perfect angle (mom decided to listen to directions for once) and my mom and teen #2 stayed safely in the raft. XD Want to see?
